pr.title: Have the release script publish the GitHub release after tagging
pr.head: 8b3c855a1821f95923dfc304bd5a6486d0901f57

summary: Cutting 0.5.0 took two commands: scripts/release.py tag pushed v0.5.0 and moved v0, and the Releases page stayed empty until someone ran gh release create by hand. This pull request makes tag finish the job.

After both tags are pushed, tag runs gh release create vX.Y.Z --repo <owner/repo> --verify-tag --generate-notes, with the repository read off the git remote. --no-release pushes only the tags. If the release step fails, the error says the tags are already pushed and prints the command that finishes the release.

cards.title: Order of operations in tag
cards.html:
StepWhat happensIf it fails
1Fetch origin/main and read the version from itNothing pushed
2Refuse if vX.Y.Z already existsNothing pushed
3Push vX.Y.Z, then force-push v0Tags may be partly pushed
4gh release create, new in this PRTags stay; error prints the finishing command

groups.title: The release step in scripts/release.py
groups.kicker: Two new functions and one new flag.
intro: repo_slug turns a git remote URL into owner/repo, and create_release uses it to call gh release create with --verify-tag, so GitHub refuses rather than inventing a tag if the push did not land.

tag calls create_release last, after both tag pushes. The tags are what the marketplaces and the walkthroughs action follow, so they must not wait on the release. A failure is re-raised with a message naming the pushed tags and the command to finish.
concepts: Once the tags are pushed, rerunning tag refuses with "already exists", so the printed command is the only path to finishing a failed release.
The release step needs an authenticated gh; the tag steps need only git.

checks.text: create_release runs only after both git push calls succeed, so a failure there never leaves the release ahead of its tag.
--no-release reaches tag as github_release=False and returns before any gh call.
The finishing command in the error omits --repo, so it works only when run from inside the checkout; adding --repo <owner/repo> when the slug is known makes it work anywhere.
repo_slug duplicates the function of the same name in skills/walkthrough-pr/scripts/walkthrough.py; a fix to remote parsing would have to land in both.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The release call is stubbed; tags still go to a temporary bare remote.
intro: TagTests.setUp patches create_release to record calls, so no test reaches GitHub. Three new tests cover the release for the exact tag, --no-release, and the failure message with the tags left in place, and a new class covers repo_slug.

checks.text: The failure test asserts both the message and that v0.5.0 is still on the remote afterwards.

groups.title: Release guide
intro: The "Release an update" section now says tag also creates the GitHub release with generated notes, that this needs an authenticated gh, how --no-release skips it, and what a failure prints.
